question: What has changed at Merrill since the start of the year?

claims.text: Merrill: a1.MER has nothing to report under leadership/management changes; the code gap records this.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill announced new data analytics fees for third-party asset managers on actively managed products, effective January 1, 2027: asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios; data on passive ETFs managed through Merrill's platforms will cost between $25,000 and $550,000. Why it might matter: the same report notes the fees are being levied on an absolute basis rather than as a percentage of assets, "making a huge nut for small firms to crack."

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill introduced a new negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee' on assets that third-party managers manage on behalf of Merrill advisors, effective January 1, 2027: up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds managed on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% on high-net-worth and ultra-high-net-worth assets to a maximum 0.1% on third-party mutual funds, money market funds, and active ETFs. Why it might matter: the report notes Merrill "made sure the scale of its squeeze on asset managers is comparable to that of its peers," citing Wells' data analytics fees of up to $1.15 million and UBS charges between $150,000 and $300,000.

Merrill: A September 15, 2026 press release states Merrill announced the launch of the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services combining automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment into managed or custom managed investment strategies in the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program; both are available through IAP and implemented by Managed Account Advisors LLC. Why it might matter: head of Fiduciary Programs and Platforms Jay Link said these services help clients "stay focused on their long-term financial goals."

Merrill: A November 16, 2026 trade report states Merrill returned to veteran broker recruiting after having largely pulled back from it at the end of 2017, returning after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf (who took over in 2023) restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. Why it might matter: the report states Merrill executives in October touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year.

Merrill: On the October 14, 2026 conference call, the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities, according to Eric Schimpf's remarks. Why it might matter: the same passage notes Merrill did not mention new AI tools even while client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the third quarter of 2026.

Merrill: According to Wolfe Research data, Merrill/Bank of America had a net loss of 552 advisors this year through August 13, the largest net advisor loss among firms. Why it might matter: the same August 2026 analysis of regulatory filings shows LPL Financial had the highest net gain of advisors at 378 and Raymond James at 293, making the 552 loss the largest on a relative basis.

Merrill: On the 2Q26 earnings call, the CFO stated advisor attrition is now at near historic lows, while saying management wants to keep growing the sales force. Why it might matter: the CFO said "We've got more to do... over the course of the next 3 to 5 years" but "we feel like we're off to a good start."

Merrill: On September 15, 2026, Merrill announced the launch of the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET), a new service that helps clients transition appreciated securities into a managed investment strategy in IAP over time while managing the realization of capital gains, with a structured tax-efficient approach. Why it might matter: Jay Link described the challenge it addresses — transitioning appreciated assets "without realizing all of the tax impact at once."

Merrill: On September 15, 2026, Merrill announced the launch of the Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), designed for clients who hold cash balances and want to gradually invest cash into a managed or custom managed investment strategy in IAP according to a client-selected schedule. Why it might matter: Jay Link explained it helps clients "invest cash without feeling pressured to time the market."

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill's new data analytics fees will cost asset managers between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for data on actively managed products, including ETFs, mutual funds, annuities and model portfolios. Why it might matter: the report notes the fees are levied on an absolute basis, not as a percentage of assets.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill's new data analytics fees on passive ETFs managed through Merrill's platforms will cost between $25,000 and $550,000. Why it might matter: this is in addition to the $125,000 to $860,000 per-firm, per-year fees on actively managed products.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill's new negotiable revenue-sharing 'support fee' will cost up to $1 million for every $1 billion of funds an asset manager manages on behalf of Merrill advisors, with fees ranging from 0.02% to a maximum 0.1%. Why it might matter: the report notes the scale of the squeeze is comparable to peers, referencing Wells, UBS and Morgan Stanley fees.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states the Bank of America subsidiary is making it possible for third-party managers to pay more for data visibility and shelf placement, effective January 1, 2027. Why it might matter: the report quotes Merrill Lynch stating in Form ADV updates that it will have a financial incentive to make available and recommend products from firms that pay data analytics fees over those that do not.

Merrill: In updates to its Form ADV, Merrill Lynch states it will have a financial incentive to make available and recommend products from third-party firms that pay fees for data analytics over those that do not, though the company says broker incentives will not shift. Why it might matter: the disclosure accompanies the new data analytics fees effective January 1, 2027.

Merrill: As of the quarter ended June 30, 2026, the Global Wealth & Investment Management franchise (which includes Merrill) continued to benefit from new AI-enabled tools that help advisers prepare for client conversations, identify opportunities and deliver more personalized advice at scale. Why it might matter: the same 2Q26 transcript reports segment net income increased 42% year-over-year to $1.4 billion and revenue grew 16% to a record $6.9 billion.

Merrill: In Q1 2026, the Global Wealth & Investment Management (GWIM) segment's noninterest expense increased $279 million to $4.9 billion, attributed primarily to higher revenue-related incentives (incentive compensation tied to revenue production). Why it might matter: the same Q1 2026 10-Q notes the segment's return on average allocated capital was 24%, up from 21%.

Merrill: In Q2 2026, the GWIM segment's noninterest expense increased $383 million to $5.0 billion, attributed primarily to higher revenue-related incentives. Why it might matter: the same Q2 2026 10-Q notes asset management fees increased 19% to $4.4 billion on higher market valuations and positive AUM flows.

Merrill: In Q3 2026, the GWIM segment's noninterest expense of $5.0 billion increased 9%, driven primarily by revenue-related incentives. Why it might matter: the same Q3 2026 press release notes pretax margin improved to 29% and return on average allocated capital reached 28%.

Merrill: A November 16, 2026 trade report states Merrill returned to veteran broker recruiting after Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf (who took over in 2023) restored a focus on hiring and a more aggressive offer. Why it might matter: the report states the firm had largely pulled back from veteran broker recruiting at the end of 2017.

Merrill: A November 16, 2026 trade report states Merrill executives in October 2026 touted that recruited assets to the wealth unit doubled year-over-year as the firm returned to veteran broker recruiting, having largely pulled back from it at the end of 2017 before Co-Presidents Lindsay Hans and Eric Schimpf restored a focus on hiring. Why it might matter: the report frames the return as a reversal of the 2017 pullback, marking a firm-level strategic shift in hiring.

Merrill: A September 11, 2026 trade report states Merrill reported the largest net losses among advisors this year through August 13, 2026, at 552, according to Wolfe Research, even as it ramped up advisor recruiting efforts. Why it might matter: the same report notes Merrill's wins came alongside teams joining from Morgan Stanley, Truist and Wells Fargo overseeing a combined $1.8 billion.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill created new data analytics fees (between $125,000 and $860,000 per-firm, per-year for actively managed products) and a revenue-sharing 'support fee' of up to 0.1% of assets, effective January 1, 2027, for third-party asset managers. Why it might matter: the report states the fees will give third parties that pay a leg up over competing firms that decline to pay.

Merrill: A September 15, 2026 press release states Merrill launched the Tax Efficient Transition Service (TET) and Dollar Cost Averaging Service (DCA), new services combining automation with professional portfolio oversight to help clients simplify asset transitions and cash deployment. Why it might matter: the release states both services are available through the Merrill Lynch Investment Advisory Program.

Merrill: On the October 14, 2026 conference call, Eric Schimpf, president and co-head of Merrill Wealth Management, said client sales of alternative investments increased 19% in the third quarter of 2026. Why it might matter: the same passage notes the message was clear that the firm would continue to invest in AI and digital capabilities.

Merrill: In the third quarter of 2026 (period ended September 30, 2026), Merrill Wealth Management client balances reached $4.2 trillion and AUM balances reached $1.9 trillion, with about 4.2K net new $500K+ households added in 3Q26. Why it might matter: the same Q3 2026 press release notes 87% of Merrill households are digitally active and 70K digital appointments were scheduled in the quarter.

Merrill: On October 2, 2026, Merrill agreed to pay $39 million to settle a class action lawsuit alleging it paid brokerage clients close-to-zero interest rates instead of market rates on cash in retirement accounts; Merrill Lynch denied wrongdoing. Why it might matter: the settlement is on top of a $25 million penalty the SEC imposed in January 2025 for not paying clients appropriate interest.

Merrill: On October 16, 2026, Merrill Lynch agreed to a settlement with state securities regulators (NASAA, led by Massachusetts) over charges of unreasonable commissions on small-dollar retail equity transactions, facing restitution on approximately $549,000 in excess commissions. Why it might matter: the settlement covers transactions from September 30, 2020 through October 1, 2025, and affected customers will receive restitution plus interest, with all three firms also paying administrative fines and investigation costs.

Merrill: A September 29, 2026 trade report states Merrill created new data analytics fees and revenue-sharing 'support' fees for third-party asset managers, disclosed in updates to its Form ADV, effective January 1, 2027. Why it might matter: the report states the disclosure acknowledges a financial incentive to recommend products from firms that pay data analytics fees over those that do not.

adjacent.text: Merrill: For the first quarter of 2026, the firm reported net client flows of $20,372 million into assets under management (the GWIM segment, which includes Merrill Wealth Management and Bank of America Private Bank), per the AUM rollforward; the definition of net client AUM flows is the net change in clients' AUM balances over a specified period, excluding market appreciation/depreciation and other adjustments.
adjacent.differs_because: The passages report 'net client flows' into assets under management (managed assets) rather than a 'net new assets' metric; net client flows cover only AUM, not total net new client assets, and are reported for the GWIM segment (Merrill plus Private Bank), not Merrill alone.
